To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the protective effect of stannic chloride on renal function in K2CrO4-treated rats was associated with the expression of HO-1; (b) the expression of HO-l was not related to other antioxidant enzymes; and (c) SnCl2 has preventive but not therapeutic effect on renal injury induced by K2 Cr2O7.
the protective effect observed in the present work is associated with the induction and activation of HO-1 and not with other enzymes.
SnCl2 pretreatment prevents K2Cr2 O7-induced renal damage by increasing the renal expression of HO-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the protective effect of the preinduction of HO-1 by SnCl2 on the renal damage induced by a single dose of K2Cr2.
the protective effect of a chemical compound on a renal injury induced by another chemical compound.
the role of HO-1 in the protection against K2Cr2 O7-induced nephroxicity and the indispensability of its preinduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SnCl2 is a potent inducer of HO-1 in the kidney and this induction is indispensable before the exposure to the toxic agent.

the protective effect observed after pretreatment with SnCl2 is not associated with the induction or the activity of antioxidant enzymes (Cu, Zn-SOD, MnSOD, GPx and CAT) but with the induction of HO-1.
the protective effect on K2CrO7-induced renal damage is due to the HO-1 induction by SnCl2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SnCl2 pretreatment protects the kidney from K2Cr2-7-induced renal injury through HO-1 pre-induction.
SnCl2 has no therapeutic effect on K2CrO7-induced nephropathy and the protective effect of this metal on K2Cr7O7-induced nephrotic syndrome is associated with the induction HO-1.

HO-1 is a key enzyme in the protective effect of stannum compounds against Cr(VI)-induced renal toxicity and the protective effect of these compounds on renal function is associated with HO activity and not with the activity of other antioxidant enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SnCl2 pretreatment is effective in protecting rats from K2Cr2- induced renal damage.
the induction of HO-1 before K2CrO4 treatment is a key event in the protective effect of stannic chloride.
HO-1 induction before K2CrO7 injection is indispensable for the protective effect of the SnCl2 on the K2Cr2-O7-induced renal damage.
